title: Engine Oil Filter Housing Change Following Transfer of the Casting Source
abstract: Requalification of the oil filter housing after the original foundry closed, with a change of casting alloy, revised mounting and a new heat shield that the different thermal expansion of the replacement material makes necessary.

sections.reason: The foundry that produced the oil filter housing casting closed in 2020 with no transfer of the pattern equipment. The replacement source could not reproduce the original alloy to the qualified process, so the housing had to be requalified on a different aluminium alloy with a higher coefficient of thermal expansion. That change is invisible at aircraft level but it moves the housing relative to its heat shield by nearly two millimetres across the operating temperature range, which the original clearances did not allow for.
sections.description: The housing is produced in the replacement alloy with a revised mounting arrangement. The clamp kit D7920122286375 is replaced by an item with a longer slot at the aft attachment, and the inboard mount link D7920124662661 is retained but shimmed at assembly. The heat shield PED599919-30 is replaced by an item with a larger relief around the filter bowl, and the forward clamp ZED715928-89 is renewed. The cowl latch CAD307983-03 at the access panel is unchanged. Plain washers EN229783-6C are used at every mount position to control the joint stack. The seal at FIN 14EO, the shroud at FIN 5656EO, the mount link at FIN 63EO and the firewall panel at FIN 7814EO are all disturbed and refitted; only the seal is renewed as a matter of course. Installation is in zones 431, 444, 452 and 454. Revised detail is on drawing D79201258552.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 1.1 kg per engine, four engines per aircraft. No electrical load change. The replacement housing is interchangeable with the original at engine level provided the revised heat shield and clamp kit are fitted with it; mixing the new housing with the original heat shield is not permitted and is called out as a caution in the installation task. No despatch or performance effect. Illustrated parts content for the oil filter housing changes, and the housing removal and installation tasks both need the new torque and shim values.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN T00206 in September 2023 and available for retrofit through a supplier service bulletin. In service the change happens naturally as housings are consumed from spares; operators wanting a uniform fleet standard can do it at engine shop visit with no aircraft downtime.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric across four engines, no reportable effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN T00206; casting lead time drove a fourteen-month qualification programme
